$comment: One event of the durable attempt journal. Every event carries the same envelope -- who called, under which capability contract, against which causal state -- and each event type adds the fields only it can supply. The envelope is not a convention: scripts/lib/wv-attempt-journal.sh builds it in one place so a call site cannot emit a partial event, and this schema is what says which fields that is. A reader (E1, the adjudication overlay, a Rust port) must never re-derive a classification the emitter already resolved.

unavailable.$comment: The shared shape for a fact that could not be obtained. It is emitted instead of a guess, and it is never the empty string or a zero.

identity.$comment: The composite causal identity, or an explicit unavailable marker. Never absent: a missing identity and an unobtainable one are different facts.

policy.$comment: The call's policy provenance, stated explicitly on every completion. applicable_rules is what the policy contract says can decide inside this operation (contracts/policy-rules-v1.json, host_event scopes excluded); evaluated_rules is what this call recorded a verdict for. A call with no verdict is NOT an allow. countable is true only when the two sets are equal, the journal itself holds a verdict for every evaluated rule, and the call ran in evidence mode; state is then 'complete'. 'unavailable' means no applicable rule spoke, 'partial' that some did not, and 'inconsistent' that a verdict names a rule the contract does not apply here or the marker and journal disagree.

oneOf.$comment: A countable call: every applicable rule decided, durably.
Anything short of that is recorded, never counted.

parent_call_id.$comment: The enclosing wv call when this call was launched underneath another, null when it is a root. Nullable rather than absent: a reader must be able to distinguish a call with no parent from a writer that does not record parents.

policy_identity.$comment: The policy contract identity (scripts/weave_policy.py identity, sha256-prefixed), bound separately from registry_identity: the registry says what an operation touches, the policy contract what may refuse it, and a reader must be able to tell which one changed. Empty only when no policy projection was sourced.

bypass.$comment: The flag or knob that overrode a condition the rule would otherwise have denied. Present only on a bypassed verdict, whose decision records what was allowed.

clause.$comment: The values a SQLite-owned close rule decided on, copied from the close receipt that the same write transaction evaluated (scripts/lib/wv-db.sh _policy_close_receipt_sql). It is the decision's own record, never a diagnosis re-derived after it, so a later change to thresholds or exemptions cannot alter it.

category.$comment: A refusal that is not a policy decision. The values are contracts/policy-rules-v1.json non_policy_categories; tests/test-policy-contract.sh keeps the two equal.

oneOf.$comment: Written before dispatch. Its disposition is incomplete and stays incomplete unless a completion follows, which is what makes a killed call visible.
A gate that decided inside the call. rule, decision and would_violate_invariant are all required: E1 cannot count a mutation whose verdict names no rule or leaves the invariant question open.
A call refused for a reason that is not policy: malformed input, a lost race, or a failure to evaluate. Recorded so a refusal is never mistaken for a counterweight decision, and never for silence.
What a mutation-class call did to durable state, derived from the two identities rather than declared.
The call ended. policy states the call's policy provenance explicitly, so no reader infers an allow from an absent verdict.
